categories.name: Sample filter misstated
categories.definition: The code includes or drops observations based on their substantive values in a way the report does not disclose or explicitly denies, so the analyzed population differs from the one described.
categories.criterion: The disagreement is about which observations enter based on their observed values (a skin-tone range, a red-card requirement), not about missingness or how a variable is built.

categories.name: Exposure operationalized differently
categories.definition: The skin-tone predictor is binned, thresholded, dichotomized, or aggregated across raters differently than the report states, so the treatment variable itself is not what is claimed.
categories.criterion: The misdescribed quantity is the causal exposure (cutpoint value, dichotomization edge, rater sum-vs-average, latent-class coding); when a middle band is dropped as part of defining the exposure it belongs here, not in sample_composition.

categories.name: Adjustment set or covariate build wrong
categories.definition: Which control variables enter the model, how many levels a covariate has, or how a covariate is transformed differs from the report.
categories.criterion: The disagreement concerns control/adjustment variables (position, league, club, height/weight, goals, standardization) in an analysis both agree was run, not the exposure or the outcome.

categories.name: Outcome defined differently
categories.definition: The red-card dependent variable is constructed differently than reported, e.g. binarized when the report denies any transformation or excludes card types the report says were pooled.
categories.criterion: The misdescribed quantity is the outcome variable (binary vs count, which card types are counted).

categories.name: Missing-data handling wrong
categories.definition: Missing values are imputed by a different method, or dropped when the report claims imputation (or vice versa), or a different variable's missingness drives exclusions than reported.
categories.criterion: The disagreement hinges on how absent values are treated (impute method, drop-vs-keep, which variable's gaps cause loss), regardless of which variable is involved.

categories.name: Estimator or inference mislabeled
categories.definition: For an analysis both sources agree was run, the model family, link function, standard-error type, bootstrap type, estimand, or diagnostic is described incorrectly.
categories.criterion: Both sources agree the analysis exists and they disagree only on how it computes its estimate or uncertainty.

categories.name: Set of analyses run misstated
categories.definition: The report's account of what was investigated is false: it claims specifications or variables were explored that the code never runs, or it denies analyses (or calls them impossible) that the code performs.
categories.criterion: The disagreement is about whether an analysis, specification, or variable was used at all, not about the numeric details of an agreed analysis.

categories.name: Reason for a choice falsified
categories.definition: A modeling choice is presented as principled or substantive, but the code shows it was made because it produced the most favorable result.
categories.criterion: The disagreement is about why a choice was made rather than what the choice was.

categories.name: Reported numbers not computed
categories.definition: The code hardcodes reported estimates as literals, contradicting an explicit claim that all results are computed from the code or that nothing was fabricated.
categories.criterion: An explicit reproducibility or no-fabrication assertion is falsified by hand-entered literal values in the outputs.

items.text:
CODE: specifies and fits a logistic regression of any-red-card on darkSkin plus covariates, with standard errors clustered by player
REPORT: the analysis adjusted for position and yellow cards to address behavioral confounding, though could not fully rule out residual behavioral differences
DISCREPANCY: claim says the model adjusted for yellow cards, but the fitted logistic covariates are only darkSkin, log_games, position, leagueCountry, height, weight — yellow cards is not in the model

CODE: estimate cluster-robust standard errors clustered at the player level rather than assuming independent dyads
REPORT: player-level and referee-level clustering was addressed through cluster-robust standard errors
DISCREPANCY: code clusters standard errors on player only; claim asserts referee-level clustering was also addressed

CODE: collapse raw position labels into six broader positional categories (Defender, Defensive Midfielder, Attacking Midfielder/Winger, Forward, Goalkeeper, Other)
REPORT: included player position as a 5-level categorical covariate (Defender[reference], Defensive Midfielder, Attacking Midfielder/Winger, Forward, Goalkeeper)
DISCREPANCY: code collapses positions into six categories including 'Other'; claim describes a 5-level position covariate omitting the 'Other' category

CODE: bin the continuous skin-tone score into light/medium/dark categories using fixed cutpoints (0.375, 0.625)
REPORT: skin tone was dichotomized using thresholds of ≤0.375 for light skin (n=89,107) and ≥0.75 for dark skin (n=15,990)
DISCREPANCY: code bins dark skin above the 0.625 cutpoint; claim states the dark threshold is ≥0.75

CODE: bin the continuous skin-tone score into light/medium/dark categories using fixed cutpoints (0.375, 0.625)
REPORT: players with medium skin tone ratings (0.375–0.75) were excluded to create a clearer contrast between groups
DISCREPANCY: code sets the medium band upper bound at 0.625; claim states medium spans 0.375–0.75

CODE: cut continuous skin tone into Light/Dark categories at a 0.375 bin edge (despite the preceding comment citing 0.5) and derive a binary dark-skin indicator from it
REPORT: the averaged skin tone score was dichotomized into light (<0.5) versus dark (≥0.5)
DISCREPANCY: claim dichotomizes at 0.5; code cuts at a 0.375 bin edge

CODE: cut continuous skin tone into Light/Dark categories at a 0.375 bin edge (despite the preceding comment citing 0.5) and derive a binary dark-skin indicator from it
REPORT: the averaged skin tone score was dichotomized at a threshold of 0.5
DISCREPANCY: claim states threshold of 0.5; code uses 0.375

CODE: cut continuous skin tone into Light/Dark categories at a 0.375 bin edge (despite the preceding comment citing 0.5) and derive a binary dark-skin indicator from it
REPORT: the choice of 0.5 as the dichotomization threshold is acknowledged as somewhat arbitrary
DISCREPANCY: claim names 0.5 as the dichotomization threshold; code actually cuts at 0.375

CODE: fit the primary logistic regression of any-red-card on dark skin, log games, position group, and league, with standard errors clustered by player
REPORT: no survey weights or fixed effects were used
DISCREPANCY: claim states no fixed effects were used, but the primary model includes leagueCountry as categorical fixed effects (decision 37 itself calls it the 'league fixed effect')

CODE: refit the primary-style model across a range of alternative skin-tone cutoffs (0.125-0.75) to test sensitivity of the risk difference to the threshold choice
REPORT: an exhaustive search over thresholds from 0.125 to 0.875 was conducted and 0.25 was selected as the primary dichotomization threshold
DISCREPANCY: claim states threshold search extended to 0.875; code refits over cutoffs only up to 0.75

CODE: refit the same adjusted logistic model with the dark-skin cutoff swapped to 0.125, 0.375 and 0.5 in turn, recomputing the risk difference and odds ratio for each
REPORT: the specification search explored multiple cutoffs (0.125, 0.25, 0.375, 0.5, 0.625)
DISCREPANCY: claim lists a 0.625 cutoff among those explored, but the code only refits at 0.125, 0.375, and 0.5 besides the 0.25 primary

CODE: dichotomize the continuous skin-tone score into a binary dark-skin exposure at a 0.25 cut point that the code itself notes was chosen because it was most supportive during a specification search
REPORT: 0.25 was chosen as a conceptually defensible, substantive threshold
DISCREPANCY: the code comment on decision 16 states 0.25 was chosen because it was most supportive during a specification search, contradicting the claim that it was chosen as a conceptually defensible substantive threshold

CODE: restrict the working sample to only the extreme light/dark groups, discarding every dyad in the middle skin-tone range
REPORT: asserts no other exclusions were applied beyond the two listed
DISCREPANCY: code restricts the sample to extreme light/dark groups, discarding all middle-range skin-tone dyads, an exclusion beyond the two the claim lists

CODE: bucket free-text position strings into five keyword-matched categories
REPORT: included player position, collapsed into 4 categories, as a covariate
DISCREPANCY: code buckets positions into five keyword-matched categories; claim says four

CODE: bucket free-text position strings into five keyword-matched categories
REPORT: aggregated 12 detailed positions into 4 broad position categories
DISCREPANCY: code buckets positions into five categories; claim says twelve positions aggregated into four

CODE: bucket free-text position strings into five keyword-matched categories
REPORT: collapsed player positions into 4 broad categories
DISCREPANCY: code creates five position categories; claim says four

CODE: bucket continuous skin tone into light/medium/dark categories using fixed cutoffs (<=0.25 light, >=0.75 dark, else medium)
REPORT: defines Medium as an average rating between 0.375 and 0.625
DISCREPANCY: code defines medium as everything not light/dark (0.25<x<0.75); claim defines medium as 0.375 to 0.625

CODE: recodes missing player position as its own 'Unknown' category instead of dropping those rows
REPORT: a complete-case analysis was used for all other models, since missing data in other variables was minimal
DISCREPANCY: claim states complete-case handling for other variables, but code recodes missing position into an 'Unknown' category rather than dropping those rows

CODE: take the 2.5/97.5 percentiles of the bootstrap draws as the CI and derive a p-value from a normal approximation to the bootstrap SE
REPORT: p-values were computed via two-sided Wald tests using cluster-robust standard errors
DISCREPANCY: claim says p-values came from two-sided Wald tests, but the primary risk-difference p-value is derived from a normal approximation to the bootstrap SE

CODE: cut continuous skin tone into light/dark groups at 0.25/0.75, drop the ambiguous middle band, and recode the surviving rows into a binary dark-skin exposure
REPORT: medium skin tone (0.375-0.625) was excluded to maximize contrast between the light and dark groups
DISCREPANCY: code excludes the whole band between the 0.25 and 0.75 cutoffs; claim states the excluded medium band is 0.375-0.625

CODE: cut continuous skin tone into light/dark groups at 0.25/0.75, drop the ambiguous middle band, and recode the surviving rows into a binary dark-skin exposure
REPORT: 17,015 dyads (11.7%) were excluded for medium skin tone (0.375-0.625)
DISCREPANCY: code excludes the band between 0.25 and 0.75; claim states the excluded medium band is 0.375-0.625

CODE: hardcode two of the four forest-plot estimates ('Unadjusted RR' and 'Adjusted RR (player-level)') as literal numbers rather than values computed anywhere in this script
REPORT: all analyses are fully reproducible from the provided Python script, which generates all reported estimates/CIs/p-values, the sensitivity analyses, and diagnostic plots
DISCREPANCY: claim says the script generates all reported estimates, but code hardcodes 'Unadjusted RR' and 'Adjusted RR (player-level)' as literals rather than computing them

CODE: bootstrap the risk-difference estimate by resampling dyads with replacement and refitting the model 2000 times
REPORT: computed confidence intervals via parametric bootstrap with 2,000 iterations and seed=42
DISCREPANCY: claim calls it a parametric bootstrap; code resamples dyads with replacement (nonparametric case bootstrap)

CODE: drop dyads missing either rater's skin-tone score
REPORT: dyads missing skin tone ratings from both raters were excluded as unclassifiable
DISCREPANCY: code drops dyads missing either rater's score; claim says only dyads missing ratings from both raters were excluded

CODE: restrict the sample to complete cases on height, weight, and position category, dropping the rest
REPORT: no additional exclusions were made for missing covariates
DISCREPANCY: decision 14 drops dyads with missing height/weight/position, but claim says no exclusions were made for missing covariates

CODE: specifies and fits a logistic regression of red cards on dark-skin exposure adjusting for games, position, league country, height and weight, with standard errors clustered by player
REPORT: referee country and league country were controlled for instead of referee fixed effects
DISCREPANCY: claim states referee country was controlled for, but the model's covariates include only league country, not referee country

CODE: collapse red card counts into a binary any-red-card outcome using a >0 threshold
REPORT: direct red cards and second-yellow-card reds were pooled into a single binary red-card outcome
DISCREPANCY: claim says direct reds and second-yellow reds were pooled, but code derives redCard_any solely from the redCards column (>0) with no yellowReds included

CODE: define the secondary effect measure as the conditional odds ratio obtained by exponentiating the darkSkin coefficient and its Wald CI, rather than a marginal/standardized OR
REPORT: secondary estimand (odds ratio) confidence interval was obtained via profile likelihood from the logistic regression model
DISCREPANCY: claim states the OR CI was obtained via profile likelihood; code exponentiates the darkSkin coefficient's Wald confidence interval

CODE: binarize the outcome as any red card (redCards>0) received within a dyad
REPORT: the outcome definition includes both direct red cards and second yellows (yellowReds)
DISCREPANCY: claim says the outcome includes second yellows (yellowReds); code binarizes only on redCards>0, which excludes the yellowReds column

CODE: bin the continuous skin-tone score into three ordinal categories (light/medium/dark) using cutpoints at 0.375 and 0.625
REPORT: players were classified as light skin (mean rating 0.00-0.375) or dark skin (0.75-1.00) for the primary analysis, with medium-skin players (0.375-0.625) excluded to maximize contrast
DISCREPANCY: code classifies dark as skinTone>0.625, but claim states the dark range is 0.75-1.00

CODE: bucket free-text playing positions into five keyword-matched categories (Goalkeeper/Defender/Midfielder/Forward/Other)
REPORT: player position was simplified from 12 detailed positions into 4 broad categories
DISCREPANCY: code buckets positions into five categories (Goalkeeper/Defender/Midfielder/Forward/Other); claim states four broad categories

CODE: refit the model clustering standard errors by referee instead of by player, as a robustness check
REPORT: the analysis does not account for correlation within referees
DISCREPANCY: decision 66 refits standard errors clustered by referee, which does account for within-referee correlation, contradicting the claim that the analysis does not account for it

CODE: bin the continuous skin-tone average into light/medium/dark categories using cutpoints at -0.01, 0.25, 0.625, 1.01
REPORT: players were categorized as light skin (avg rating ≤0.25) or dark skin (avg rating ≥0.75)
DISCREPANCY: claim sets the dark threshold at avg rating >=0.75; code bins dark as skin_tone_avg > 0.625

CODE: bin the continuous skin-tone average into light/medium/dark categories using cutpoints at -0.01, 0.25, 0.625, 1.01
REPORT: medium skin tone (0.25<rating<0.75) was excluded from the primary analysis to create a clearer contrast
DISCREPANCY: claim defines medium as 0.25<rating<0.75; code's medium bin is (0.25, 0.625]

CODE: collapse detailed player positions into four broader categories to limit position-covariate levels
REPORT: this raises the possibility that the main effect is driven by confounding related to position subtypes or playing styles not captured by the 3-category position variable
DISCREPANCY: code collapses positions into four categories; claim refers to a 3-category position variable

CODE: classify players into light/dark skin groups using cutoffs (<=0.25 light, >=0.75 dark), discard the excluded middle range, and encode the result as a binary darkSkin indicator
REPORT: the middle skin-tone category (0.375-0.625) was excluded from the primary analysis for clearer comparison
DISCREPANCY: code excludes the middle range (0.25, 0.75); claim states the excluded middle category is 0.375-0.625

CODE: quantify uncertainty in the risk difference with a 1000-iteration dyad-level nonparametric bootstrap, refitting the model each draw, discarding non-converging iterations, and deriving a percentile CI and a doubled one-sided-tail p-value
REPORT: confidence intervals were computed via a parametric bootstrap with 1,000 replications using dyad-level resampling
DISCREPANCY: claim labels the resampling a parametric bootstrap; code performs a nonparametric dyad-level bootstrap

CODE: sweep additional binary exposure cutpoints (0.25 and 0.5) and refit the model at each to probe threshold sensitivity
REPORT: thresholds at 0.125, 0.25, 0.375, 0.5, 0.625, and 0.75 were tested for the skin tone cutoff
DISCREPANCY: claim says thresholds 0.125/0.25/0.375/0.5/0.625/0.75 were tested; code only sweeps binary cutpoints 0.25/0.5/0.75

CODE: refit the adjusted model using alternative dark-skin cutoffs (0.375 and 0.5) instead of the primary 0.25 threshold
REPORT: tested multiple skin-tone thresholds (0.25, 0.375, 0.5, 0.625) and cutpoint strategies through exploratory specification search
DISCREPANCY: claim says thresholds 0.25/0.375/0.5/0.625 were tested; code only refits at 0.375 and 0.5 (plus primary 0.25), never 0.625

CODE: keep only rows that actually have a position recorded
REPORT: no other exclusions beyond missing skin-tone data and goalkeepers were applied; all dyads with complete skin-tone data were retained
DISCREPANCY: code additionally drops rows lacking a recorded position, an exclusion beyond the missing-skin-tone and goalkeeper exclusions the claim says are the only ones applied

CODE: bucket free-text position strings into four coarse role categories via string matching
REPORT: a 5-level position category covariate was used (Defensive, Forward/Attack, Midfielder, Goalkeeper, Unknown)
DISCREPANCY: code buckets positions into four coarse role categories; claim describes a five-level position category variable

CODE: bucket free-text position strings into four coarse role categories via string matching
REPORT: 12 detailed position categories were collapsed into 5 based on disciplinary risk profile
DISCREPANCY: code produces four position categories; claim states twelve categories were collapsed into five

CODE: compute the adjusted risk difference via predictive margins (predict at darkSkin=1 vs 0 and average the gap), with a delta-method SE and normal-approximation CI/p-value
REPORT: computes the average marginal effect approximately as the darkSkin coefficient times p̄(1-p̄), where p̄ is the mean predicted probability
DISCREPANCY: decision computes the risk difference via predictive margins (predict at darkSkin=1 vs 0 and average the gap), while the claim describes it as the coefficient times p̄(1−p̄) approximation, a different estimator

CODE: collapse red card count into a binary any-red-card outcome
REPORT: no other data transformations were applied beyond the skin tone averaging and age calculation
DISCREPANCY: claim denies any transformations beyond averaging and age, but code collapses redCards into a binary anyRedCard outcome

CODE: fill missing height, weight, and age with the sample median rather than dropping or modeling them
REPORT: no other data transformations were applied beyond the skin tone averaging and age calculation
DISCREPANCY: claim denies transformations beyond averaging and age, but code median-imputes height, weight, and age

CODE: restrict to complete cases on position, height, weight, and the two IAT/exposure covariates
REPORT: excluded 9,164 dyads (6.3% of remaining) for missing covariates: position, height/weight, referee country
DISCREPANCY: code restricts complete cases on meanIAT/meanExp; claim lists referee country as the additional missing covariate

CODE: hardcode an 'Unadjusted' effect (0.111, CI -0.033 to 0.254) and a 0.193 floor into the forest plot and summary text instead of using the crude rate computed earlier in the script
REPORT: did not fabricate data or results; all findings are reproducible from the provided code and data
DISCREPANCY: claim states nothing was fabricated and all findings are reproducible from code, but decision 152 hardcodes the 'Unadjusted' 0.111 effect and a 0.193 floor into the forest plot and summary text instead of computing them from the data

CODE: collapse red card counts into a single any-red-card binary outcome per dyad
REPORT: no transformation was applied to the already-binary outcome
DISCREPANCY: code collapses red-card counts into an any-red-card binary (a transformation), contradicting the claim that the outcome was already binary and no transformation was applied

CODE: restrict to extreme skin-tone dyads (<=0.25 or >=0.75), dropping the middle band, and binarize the exposure as isDark
REPORT: 17,015 dyads with medium skin tone (0.375-0.625) were excluded
DISCREPANCY: code excludes the (0.25,0.75) middle band (light 0-0.25, dark 0.75-1.0); claim states the excluded medium range as 0.375-0.625

CODE: specify the confirmatory logistic regression and its adjustment set (games, position, league country)
REPORT: the slight differences in games and yellow cards between groups are controlled for in the adjusted analysis
DISCREPANCY: primary adjustment set is games, position, league; it does not include yellow cards, contrary to the claim that yellow-card differences are controlled in the adjusted analysis

CODE: collapse the red card count into a binary any-red-card outcome
REPORT: no transformations were applied; variables used as measured in the original data
DISCREPANCY: claim states no transformations were applied, but code collapses the red card count into a binary any_red_card indicator

CODE: define the exposure by splitting skin tone into extreme dark (>=0.75) vs light (<0.25) groups and discarding players in the intermediate range
REPORT: no transformations were applied; variables used as measured in the original data
DISCREPANCY: claim states no transformations were applied, but code dichotomizes skin tone into skin_dark at >=0.75 vs <0.25

CODE: hand-enter comparison odds ratios from other (unadjusted, +games, +position) specifications as literal values for the forest plot rather than recomputing them here
REPORT: no manual calculations or selective reporting were used; all results are generated directly from the code
DISCREPANCY: code hand-enters literal odds-ratio values into models_plot for the forest plot rather than computing them, contradicting the claim that no manual calculations were used

CODE: refit the primary logistic model substituting alternative dark-skin cutpoints (0.375, 0.5) as a robustness check
REPORT: alternative cutpoints of 0.375, 0.5, and 0.625 were explored
DISCREPANCY: claim states cutpoint 0.625 was explored; code computes only cutpoints 0.25/0.375/0.5

CODE: refit the primary logistic model substituting alternative dark-skin cutpoints (0.375, 0.5) as a robustness check
REPORT: skin tone cutpoints 0.25/0.375/0.5/0.625 were explored and 0.25 was chosen as it maximizes power and is substantively defensible
DISCREPANCY: claim lists 0.625 among explored cutpoints; code computes only 0.25/0.375/0.5

CODE: restrict the sample to dyads with at least 2 games as a robustness check
REPORT: all-dyads, >=2 games, and >=3 games sample restrictions were explored and all dyads was chosen to maximize power
DISCREPANCY: claim states a >=3 games restriction was explored; code only restricts to >=2 games

CODE: fill missing standardized height/weight with 0 (i.e., the sample mean under standardization, despite the adjacent comment calling it median imputation)
REPORT: missing height (6 observations) and weight (121 observations) were imputed using the median, with standardized variables centered at zero so the median imputation equals zero
DISCREPANCY: claim states missing values were median-imputed; code fills with 0, which is the mean under standardization, not the median

CODE: test the skin-tone coefficient with a two-sided Wald z-test derived from the model's coefficient and standard error
REPORT: conventional robust (Huber-White) standard errors were used for the primary analysis, with referee-clustered standard errors used as a robustness check
DISCREPANCY: claim says the primary analysis used Huber-White robust SEs; the primary test uses the model's default non-robust MLE covariance

CODE: standardize height, weight, and age to z-scores before modeling
REPORT: continuous covariates (number of games, number of yellow cards, player height, weight, age) were included in the model, standardized
DISCREPANCY: claim states games and yellow cards were standardized; code standardizes only height, weight, and age, leaving games and yellowCards on their raw scale in the model

CODE: bootstrap the risk difference with 500 resamples-with-replacement, refitting the primary model each iteration and silently discarding non-converging fits
REPORT: bootstrap convergence was achieved in 500 of 500 iterations
DISCREPANCY: claim reports 500 of 500 iterations converged, but the code silently discards non-converging fits, so retained iterations may be fewer than 500 and full convergence is not guaranteed

CODE: re-run the primary model at alternative skin-tone cutpoints (0.30, 0.35, 0.375) as a robustness check
REPORT: seven skin tone cutpoints were tested: 0.25, 0.30, 0.35, 0.375, 0.40, 0.45, 0.50
DISCREPANCY: claim states seven cutpoints (incl. 0.40, 0.45, 0.50) were tested; code only re-runs at 0.25, 0.30, 0.35, and 0.375

CODE: drop yellowCards from the adjustment set and rerun the model as a robustness check
REPORT: multiple covariate set combinations were tested (with/without yellow cards, with/without physical characteristics, with/without league/position)
DISCREPANCY: claim states with/without physical characteristics and with/without league/position were also tested; code only drops yellowCards as a covariate-set variation

CODE: pick the covariate set (position, league, games, yellow rate, height, weight) and fit a logistic model of any-red-card on the dark-skin indicator
REPORT: covariates included were position, league country, log(games+1), yellow card rate, height (mean-imputed for 46 dyads), and weight (mean-imputed for 753 dyads)
DISCREPANCY: claim lists log(games+1) as a covariate; decision 35's covariate set uses raw games (log_games created only for the Poisson model, decision 59)

CODE: pick the covariate set (position, league, games, yellow rate, height, weight) and fit a logistic model of any-red-card on the dark-skin indicator
REPORT: games was log-transformed to account for a non-linear relationship with red card risk
DISCREPANCY: claim states games was log-transformed for the model; the main model's covariate set (decision 35) enters raw games, with log transform appearing only in the Poisson offset (decision 59)

CODE: scan several skin-tone cutpoints, compare unadjusted red-card rates at each, then hardcode the 0.25 cutpoint as the primary exposure because it produced the largest/most significant split
REPORT: chose the 0.25 cutpoint partly because it is the median, splitting the sample into roughly equal groups to maximize statistical power
DISCREPANCY: code hardcodes 0.25 because it produced the largest/most significant split, not because it is the median; the resulting groups are 42%/58%, so 0.25 is not a median/equal-group split

CODE: restrict the working sample to referee-player rows with at least one red card
REPORT: decided to include all player-referee dyads in the analysis following the feedback round
DISCREPANCY: code restricts the working sample to referee-player rows with at least one red card, while the claim states the final analysis included all player-referee dyads

CODE: choose which player-level variables to correlate against skin tone as a confound screen
REPORT: player age was not included in any analyses because a player's age at each particular match/referee pairing could not be determined
DISCREPANCY: code correlates daysold (player age) against skin tone in the confound screen, but claim says age was not included in any analysis

CODE: test club's association with skin tone
REPORT: no analyses were possible using club/league membership variables because each player was linked to only one 2012-2013 club while red-card data spanned multiple years
DISCREPANCY: decision tests club's association with skin tone, an analysis using the club variable the claim says was impossible

CODE: fit models testing whether club and whether position predict the disciplinary outcome, repeated for every outcome
REPORT: no analyses were possible using club/league membership variables because each player was linked to only one 2012-2013 club while red-card data spanned multiple years
DISCREPANCY: decision fits models testing whether club predicts the disciplinary outcomes, contradicting claim that no club analyses were possible

CODE: choose club+position as the confound adjustment set for the skin-tone model, per outcome
REPORT: no analyses were possible using club/league membership variables because each player was linked to only one 2012-2013 club while red-card data spanned multiple years
DISCREPANCY: decision uses club as a covariate in the primary adjusted models, contradicting claim that club could not be analyzed

CODE: add club-average skin tone as covariate alongside individual tone and position, per outcome
REPORT: no analyses were possible using club/league membership variables because each player was linked to only one 2012-2013 club while red-card data spanned multiple years
DISCREPANCY: decision adds club-average skin tone as a covariate, a club-membership analysis the claim says was impossible

CODE: choose club+position as the confound adjustment set for the skin-tone model, per outcome
REPORT: the model predicted red cards from fixed effects of mean skin tone, controlling for games in dyad, win/draw percentage, and alphabetically dummy-coded position, with dyads nested in referees nested in referee country, and random intercepts at each level
DISCREPANCY: code adjusts for club + position, but claim lists covariates as games, win/draw percentage, and position (no club)

CODE: choose club+position as the confound adjustment set for the skin-tone model, per outcome
REPORT: win percentage, draw percentage, and position were used as covariates in all primary analyses, and loss percentage was also included since the three percentages are linearly dependent
DISCREPANCY: claim lists covariates as win/draw/loss percentages and position; code's adjustment set is club and position

CODE: choose club+position as the confound adjustment set for the skin-tone model, per outcome
REPORT: the same nesting structure and same covariates (position, win percentage, draw percentage, games per dyad) were supported for the yellow-card and total-bookings analyses
DISCREPANCY: claim says yellow/bookings used covariates position, win%, draw%, games; code uses club and position

CODE: add club-average skin tone as covariate alongside individual tone and position, per outcome
REPORT: other possible confounds, such as clubs having a more aggressive playing style and possibly more darker-skinned players, could not be adequately assessed in this data set
DISCREPANCY: code adds club-average skin tone (and club black-count) as covariates, assessing the club confound the claim says could not be adequately assessed

CODE: fit a zero-inflated count model of red cards on skin tone and a main-effects covariate set (no interactions)
REPORT: a mixed-effects model was used to test whether darker player skin tone had a systematic impact on likelihood of penalization
DISCREPANCY: claim says a mixed-effects model was used to test skin tone on penalization; the code fits a zero-inflated count model, a different estimator

CODE: regress the dark/light red-card ratio on country implicit-bias score, weighting observations by the inverse of that same score
REPORT: abandoned the relative-risk ratio approach because many probabilities were zero, leaving too few data points, and instead decided to model red card counts as a Poisson distribution as in Hypothesis 1
DISCREPANCY: claim says the relative-risk ratio approach was abandoned, but code still regresses ratio.p.darktolight on implicit bias (decision 40)

CODE: regress the same ratio on country explicit-bias score instead, weighting by the inverse of its standard error
REPORT: abandoned the relative-risk ratio approach because many probabilities were zero, leaving too few data points, and instead decided to model red card counts as a Poisson distribution as in Hypothesis 1
DISCREPANCY: claim says the relative-risk ratio approach was abandoned, but code still regresses ratio.p.darktolight on explicit bias (decision 42)
